passages.note: House Third Reading vote page; Pingerelli voted Aye on final passage of this single-subject voter-registration/citizenship-verification bill.

Bill status page shows HB2492 signed into law as Chapter 99; it lists sponsors (not including Pingerelli) and the Governor's signature but prints neither her vote nor the operative text, so it cannot alone establish the chair.

passages.provision_quote: Except for a form produced by the United States election assistance commission, any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship.
passages.note: Enacted bill text (Chapter 99) requires documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, matching rung 5's clause exactly; this is the instrument Pingerelli voted Aye on.

rows.reasoning: Pingerelli voted Aye on final House passage of HB2492 (2022), a single-subject voter-registration/citizenship-verification bill whose enacted text requires that registration applications 'be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship,' matching the rung 'Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote.' The bill's other provisions (driver-license registration, residency proof, federal-only-voter eligibility, enforcement) all serve this one citizenship-verification scheme rather than bundling unrelated subjects.
